NONE: › an informal or child's word for stomach
（非正式的說法或兒語）胃
› to fall quickly and without control
跌倒；滾下，墜落；倒塌
› to fall a lot in value in a short time
（價值）暴跌，驟降
› to move in an uncontrolled way, as if falling or likely to fall
跌跌撞撞地走
› a sudden fall
摔倒，跌跤；跌落

example: I lost my footing and tumbled down the stairs.
我一失足從樓梯上滾了下來。
At any moment the whole building could tumble down.
整幢建築隨時有可能倒塌。
He lost his balance and tumbled over.
他失去平衡摔倒了。
Share prices tumbled yesterday.
昨天股票大跌。
An excited group of children tumbled out of school/the bus.
一群激動不已的孩子一窩蜂地跑出了學校／跑下了公車。
She took a nasty tumble on her way to work and grazed her arm.
她上班途中重重摔了一跤，擦傷了胳膊。

NONE: › a machine that dries wet clothes by turning them in hot air
滾筒式烘乾機

example: Compare
spin-dryer

NONE: › to suddenly understand something
突然明白，對…恍然大悟

example: I think he's tumbled to our plan.
我覺得他已茅塞頓開，明白了我們的計劃。

NONE: › (of a building) in a very bad condition, especially in a state of decay
（建築物）搖搖欲墜的，破敗不堪的

example: a tumbledown cottage
破敗不堪的村舍

NONE: › a drinking container that does not have a handle or a stem
（無柄無腳的）杯子
› a plant of North America and Australia that breaks near the ground when it dies, and forms large balls that are rolled around by the wind
風滾草（生長於北美和澳大利亞，枯萎後在地面處折落，隨風像球一樣四處滾動）
› (especially of parts of the body) swollen or becoming swollen
（尤指身體部位）腫脹的，腫大的，充血腫脹的

example: a tumescent penis
勃起的陰莖

NONE: › the stomach, or the lower front part of the body
胃，肚子

example: a tummy ache
肚子痛

腫瘤；腫塊

他們在她的乳房中發現了一個惡性腫瘤。
a benign tumour

NONE: › a loud noise, especially that produced by an excited crowd, or a state of confusion, change, or uncertainty
吵鬧，喧嘩；騷亂，混亂

example: You couldn't hear her speak over the tumult from the screaming fans.
在那些尖叫的歌迷的喧鬧聲中，你根本無法聽清她在說甚麼。
From every direction, people were running and shouting and falling over each other in a tumult of confusion.
在一片騷亂中，人們四處狂奔，大喊大叫，你絆倒我，我絆倒你。
The financial markets are in tumult.
金融市場一片混亂。

NONE: › very loud, or full of confusion, change, or uncertainty
吵鬧的，喧嘩的；騷亂的，混亂的

example: The former president appeared to tumultuous applause and a standing ovation.
前總統出場時，人們起立鼓掌，歡呼聲經久不息。
After the tumultuous events of 1990, Europe was completely transformed.
經歷了1990年的一系列動盪和騷亂事件後，歐洲發生了劇變。
